I can use WhatsApp and YouTube, and type slowly

plan.summary: This path takes you from basic computer skills to freelance website work in about 6 months. You'll start by getting comfortable with computers and typing, then learn how to build and style web pages, use WordPress (which many local businesses need), and manage your work with version control. Each step includes a small project you can show to potential clients. The path focuses on skills that Bhopal and nearby businesses actually pay for.

steps.title: Get comfortable with computers
steps.why: Since you're new to computers beyond WhatsApp and YouTube, you need to learn how files, folders, and basic computer operations work before anything else.

project.title: Organize a practice folder
project.brief: Create folders on your laptop for different topics (like 'Learning', 'Projects', 'Photos') and practice moving files between them.
acceptanceCriteria: You created at least 3 folders with clear names
You moved or copied at least 5 files between folders
You can find any file you saved without help

steps.title: Learn to type faster
steps.why: Typing slowly will make everything take much longer. Spending time now to type faster will save you hours every week going forward.

project.title: Reach 25 words per minute
project.brief: Practice typing every day until you can type at least 25 words per minute without looking at the keyboard much.
acceptanceCriteria: You can type 25 words per minute on a typing test
You use most of your fingers, not just two
You can type a full paragraph without many mistakes

steps.title: Understand email and online communication
steps.why: Freelance work means emailing clients, sharing files, and professional communication. You need to know how email works properly.

project.title: Set up a professional email
project.brief: Create a new email address that looks professional (like yourname@gmail.com), send a practice email to yourself with an attachment, and organize it into folders.
acceptanceCriteria: You created an email address with your real name
You sent an email with a file attached
You created at least 2 folders to organize emails

steps.title: Improve your English writing
steps.why: Freelance clients need clear communication. Better English helps you write professional emails, understand instructions, and create content.

project.title: Write a service description
project.brief: Write a short paragraph (5-6 sentences) describing a service you want to offer, like 'I build simple websites for small businesses.'
acceptanceCriteria: Your paragraph has no major grammar mistakes
Each sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with proper punctuation
Someone reading it clearly understands what you offer

steps.title: Learn how web pages are built
steps.why: HTML and CSS are the building blocks of every website. You need to understand these before you can build or fix websites for clients.

project.title: Build a simple personal page
project.brief: Create a single web page about yourself with a heading, a paragraph about your skills, a list of services you want to offer, and basic styling with colors.
acceptanceCriteria: The page has a heading, paragraph, and list
You changed at least 3 colors or fonts using CSS
The page looks readable on both your phone and laptop

steps.title: Learn WordPress for client websites
steps.why: Most small businesses in Bhopal want WordPress sites because they're easy to update. This skill gets you paying work quickly.

project.title: Build a practice business website
project.brief: Create a complete WordPress site for an imaginary local business (like a restaurant or shop) with a home page, about page, services page, and contact form.
acceptanceCriteria: The site has at least 4 pages with real content
You added a contact form that works
You chose and customized a theme so it doesn't look like the default

steps.title: Learn version control basics
steps.why: Git helps you save different versions of your work and is expected by most clients and agencies. It protects you from losing work.

project.title: Save your website code online
project.brief: Put the personal page you built earlier on GitHub so others can see your work and you have a backup.
acceptanceCriteria: You created a GitHub account
You uploaded your HTML/CSS files to a repository
You can share the link with someone to view your code

steps.title: Add interactivity with JavaScript basics
steps.why: JavaScript makes websites interactive (like buttons that do things when clicked). This skill helps you charge more and handle more client requests.

project.title: Add a simple interactive feature
project.brief: Add a button to your personal page that does something when clicked, like showing a hidden message or changing the page background color.
acceptanceCriteria: You added a button that works when clicked
Something visible on the page changes when you click it
The code works without errors in the browser console

roles.note: Building and fixing the visual/interactive part of websites, often as freelance gigs (Upwork/Fiverr-style) or a junior role at a small agency. A portfolio of 2-3 real small sites matters more than a degree here.
Setting up and customising WordPress sites for local shops, clinics and small firms in Bhopal/Indore who need a simple website but can't afford a full dev team. Usually paid per project.

roles.category: Freelance web maintenance & basic tech support
roles.note: Ongoing small fixes for existing websites (updating text/images, fixing broken pages, basic troubleshooting) for local businesses. Good recurring income once you've built 1-2 sites and earned trust.

plan.disclaimer: Disha shows categories of work and the skills they typically need, based on a curated set of free resources — it does not guarantee a job, an interview, or income.

intake.currentSkills: I know basic Excel and some English
I know basic Excel and some English

plan.summary: You'll start by strengthening your computer and English foundations, then learn SQL and Python—the core tools data analysts use daily. Next, you'll practice cleaning and analyzing data with Pandas. Finally, you'll build real mini-projects to show employers you can turn messy data into insights. This path takes about 16 weeks at 8 hours/week and prepares you for junior data analyst roles in Indore or remote positions.

steps.title: Strengthen your English communication
steps.why: Data analysts write reports and emails to explain findings. Better English helps you communicate insights clearly to managers and teammates.

project.title: Weekly Learning Journal
project.brief: Write a short paragraph in English every day about what you learned that day, as if explaining it to a friend.
acceptanceCriteria: You have 7 journal entries, each 4-5 sentences long
Each entry uses at least 2 new vocabulary words from BBC lessons
You can read your entries aloud smoothly without stumbling

steps.title: Master spreadsheets deeply
steps.why: You know basic Excel, but data analysts use advanced formulas, pivot tables, and charts daily. Google Sheets teaches these skills and is free to practice anywhere.

project.title: Personal Expense Tracker
project.brief: Create a Google Sheet tracking your monthly expenses by category (food, transport, etc.) with formulas that calculate totals and percentages.
acceptanceCriteria: Sheet has at least 20 expense entries across 4 categories
Uses SUM, AVERAGE, and percentage formulas correctly
Includes one pie chart showing spending by category

steps.title: Learn SQL to query databases
steps.why: Most company data lives in databases, not spreadsheets. SQL lets you pull exactly the data you need for analysis—it's the #1 skill employers want.

project.title: Movie Database Queries
project.brief: Using SQLBolt's practice database, write 5 different queries to answer questions like 'Which movies were released after 2010?' or 'What's the average movie rating?'
acceptanceCriteria: All 5 queries run without errors
At least one query uses WHERE to filter data
At least one query uses GROUP BY and an aggregate function like AVG or COUNT

steps.title: Start programming with Python
steps.why: Python automates repetitive tasks and handles datasets too large for spreadsheets. It's beginner-friendly and the most popular language for data analysis.

project.title: Budget Calculator Script
project.brief: Write a Python program that asks for your monthly income and expenses, then calculates how much you can save and prints a simple summary.
acceptanceCriteria: Program takes at least 3 expense inputs from the user
Calculates and displays total expenses and remaining savings
Uses variables, input(), print(), and basic math operations correctly

steps.title: Clean messy data with Pandas
steps.why: Real-world data is always messy—missing values, duplicates, wrong formats. Pandas is Python's tool for cleaning and preparing data before analysis.

project.title: Clean a Real Dataset
project.brief: Download a messy CSV dataset from Kaggle (like customer records), then use Pandas to remove duplicates, fill missing values, and fix data types.
acceptanceCriteria: You identify and document at least 3 data quality issues in the original file
Your Python script removes duplicates and handles missing values
You export a cleaned CSV and can explain what you fixed in plain English

steps.title: Analyze data with Pandas
steps.why: Now you'll use Pandas to actually answer questions from data—grouping, filtering, and calculating statistics. This is what data analysts do every day.

project.title: Sales Analysis Report
project.brief: Use a sales dataset (from Kaggle or create fake data) to answer: Which product sold most? What's the average order value? Which month had highest sales?
acceptanceCriteria: Your script calculates at least 3 different statistics (totals, averages, counts)
You use groupby() to analyze data by category or time period
You write a 1-paragraph summary of your findings in plain English

steps.title: Practice more SQL with real databases
steps.why: Employers will test your SQL skills in interviews. This certification gives you hands-on practice building and querying databases from scratch.

project.title: Student Records Database
project.brief: Design and build a small database with tables for students, courses, and enrollments. Write queries to find things like 'all students in Math' or 'courses with more than 10 students'.
acceptanceCriteria: Database has at least 3 related tables with proper foreign keys
You insert at least 15 sample records across all tables
You write 5 queries including at least one JOIN between tables

roles.note: Pulling numbers from spreadsheets/databases and turning them into simple charts or summaries a manager can act on. Entry-level roles usually want spreadsheet fluency plus basic SQL; Python/pandas is a strong plus, not always required on day one.

plan.disclaimer: Disha shows categories of work and the skills they typically need, based on a curated set of free resources — it does not guarantee a job, an interview, or income.
